evals.prompt: Create a distinctive Next.js landing page for a premium repair service. I like editorial layouts, warm neutrals, and restrained motion; avoid generic SaaS gradients. Do not do market research.
evals.expected_output: Standalone preference-led concept funnel and local Next.js build without research.

evals.prompt: Use the approved brand and customer segment to build a unique responsive marketing site. Generate a small hero-image contact sheet with FAL only after showing the estimated cost, then prepare a GitHub/Vercel Preview.
evals.expected_output: Uses approved brand constraints, approval-gated FAL build-time assets, responsive QA, and Preview workflow.

evals.prompt: Run a simple A/B test on the homepage hero CTA. Keep the design unchanged except for the CTA copy.
evals.expected_output: Declares one hypothesis/variable/metric, uses control-treatment flags, and keeps production activation gated.

evals.prompt: Build the homepage so it radiates confidence. Use a subtle amount of superlative language—enough to feel compelling, never inflated—and support it with proof.
evals.expected_output: Uses decisive, specific copy and hierarchy; applies at most a small number of earned superlatives, avoids unsupported rankings or guarantees, and places proof near the CTA.
